interestRows.studentInterest: understanding health and disease from molecules to populations
interestRows.finding: The bachelor explicitly studies health and disease across molecular, cellular, patient and population levels.

interestRows.studentInterest: why people become ill and how disease can be prevented
interestRows.finding: The programme presents explaining illness and preventing disease as central biomedical questions.

interestRows.studentInterest: improving patient care through biomedical research
interestRows.finding: Students learn to translate questions from healthcare into research and innovations that can improve care.

interestRows.studentInterest: how biological mechanisms shape human health
interestRows.finding: The programme connects molecular and cellular mechanisms to health, disease and patient problems.

interestRows.studentInterest: combining laboratory, clinical and population research
interestRows.finding: The programme identity explicitly integrates experimental laboratory research, patient-oriented work and population research.

interestRows.studentInterest: translating clinical problems into research questions
interestRows.finding: A central learning line teaches students to turn healthcare problems into answerable scientific questions.
The programme trains students to use biomedical evidence and stakeholder needs when developing healthcare innovations.

interestRows.studentInterest: working with patients and healthcare professionals
interestRows.finding: Programme material emphasises contact with patients and collaboration with healthcare professionals during biomedical study.
Molecular sciences is one of the formally identified specialisation fields available through third-year bachelor minors.
Epidemiology is a formally identified specialisation field within the third-year minor structure.
Movement sciences is one of the programme’s formally identified third-year specialisation fields.
Neuroscience is explicitly offered as a specialisation field through the bachelor’s third-year minors.
Health technology assessment is named as a field in which students can specialise through the bachelor minor structure.
Immunology is one of the programme’s formal specialisation fields in the third year.
Toxicology is explicitly listed among the fields available for specialisation through third-year minors.

interestRows.studentInterest: conducting an independent biomedical research project
interestRows.finding: The third year culminates in a twenty-week research placement in which students carry out their own biomedical project.
Statistics and quantitative analysis are embedded in the programme’s research-methods learning line.
Students are taught to evaluate scientific literature and use it to substantiate biomedical conclusions.
The curriculum explicitly addresses scientific integrity and responsible biomedical research.
The innovation learning line includes investigating the needs of patients and other stakeholders.
Students work on innovation projects that move from a care problem to a substantiated solution.
The programme teaches research at molecular and cellular levels and applies laboratory methods to health questions.
Patient-level research is a recurring component of the bachelor’s integrated research approach.
The programme teaches how health and disease can be investigated at population level.
A programme quarter uses nature and nurture as a substantive framework for understanding biomedical differences.
Homeostasis is a named curricular theme used to connect physiological regulation with health and disease.
The programme’s attack-and-defence theme studies biological threats and the body’s protective responses.

interestRows.studentInterest: human development across the life course
interestRows.finding: Life phases form a named curricular context for studying development, ageing and disease.
Neoplasms are explicitly included in a programme quarter focused on life phases and disease.
Movement is a named programme theme that connects biomedical mechanisms with human functioning.
Flow is used as a substantive curricular theme for biomedical functioning and disease.
A named programme theme focuses on how biomedical claims and healthcare decisions are supported by evidence.
Personalised care is presented as a curricular context for applying biomedical evidence to individual patients.

interestRows.finding: The programme’s career material identifies research positions in academic, hospital and public-health settings. interestRows.studentInterest: pursuing a master’s in Biomedical Sciences
interestRows.finding: The programme identifies the Biomedical Sciences master’s as a common further-study destination. Current careers information conditions outcomes on the subsequent master, further study and individual choices; this is search evidence, not a construction generator or promised qualification.
